claims.claim: Eustathius was a native of Side in Pamphylia and was previously bishop of Beroea (modern Aleppo) before becoming bishop of Antioch.
Eustathius died around 337, possibly in Thrace, after being banished there by Emperor Constantine the Great.
The Commentary on Psalm 15 (Commentarius in Psalmum) survives only as fragments.
Most of Eustathius's numerous dogmatic and exegetical treatises have been lost.
Eustathius was a zealous opponent of Arianism and defender of Nicene orthodoxy.
Eustathius was deposed by a synod of Arian prelates at Antioch in 327 or 330 and exiled to Trajanopolis in Thrace.
The resistance of Eustathius's followers in Antioch created a Eustathian faction that survived until about 485 and developed into the Meletian Schism.
Eustathius's only complete extant work is De Engastrimytho contra Origenem.
The Commentary on the Hexameron attributed to Eustathius in manuscripts is spurious, being too late to be authentic.
